title: As one that serveth (Luke 22:24–27)
hookLine: at the supper they argue about greatness; he says I am among you as one that serves
carry: servant of the servants of God

lines: RIGHT AFTER THE BREAD AND CUP.
WHICH OF US IS THE GREATER?
LUKE SETS IT AT THE SUPPER.
cards: In Luke, the very next thing after the bread and the cup is an argument. Jesus has just said this is my body, given for you. He has just said one of them will betray him.
And at that same table the apostles fall to arguing about which of them is the greater. A family bickering over the good chair at a hospital bedside.
Mark and Matthew tell of a similar quarrel earlier, on the road; Luke sets it here, at the Last Supper.

teach.b: Luke says: "And there was also a strife amongst them, which of them should seem to be the greater." Jesus doesn't scold them for wanting to matter. He redraws what mattering means.

The kings of the nations lord it over people, he says, and those in power like to be called benefactors. "But you not so." Let the greater among you become as the younger, and the leader as one who serves.
Then a simple question about the room they're in: who's greater, the one reclining at table or the one serving? At any dinner, the one at table. "But I am in the midst of you, as he that serveth."
Present tense. Right now, at this table.

teach.h: DIAKONON: THE ONE WHO WAITS TABLES.
teach.b: The Greek word is diakonon, the one who waits on tables, from the same family as the word deacon. The Catholic Church builds this into its own shape.
Every priest and bishop is first ordained a deacon, a servant, and that service is meant never to wear off.

teach.h: SERVANT OF THE SERVANTS OF GOD.
teach.b: Pope Gregory the Great called himself servant of the servants of God, servus servorum Dei, and popes still use the title at the head of official letters.

teach.h: I AM IN THE MIDST OF YOU AS HE THAT SERVETH.
teach.b: A title doesn't guarantee anyone lives up to it. It names the standard Jesus set the night before he died: greatness measured by service.

how: Every Catholic priest and bishop is first ordained a deacon, and the Holy Thursday Mass of the Lord's Supper provides for the priest to wash the feet of members of the congregation, in memory of Christ serving at the Last Supper.

games.q: your friends are arguing about which of them is most important, right at the dinner table. you're their teacher. what do you do?
o: settle it by naming the greatest.
point out you're among them as the one who serves.
games.why: he asks who's greater, the one at table or the one serving, and says I am in the midst of you as he that serveth.

practice: Picture the rooms you'll be in today, home, work, a bus, a store, and find one small job nobody wants: dishes in the sink, a full trash bag, a tired parent, a coworker drowning in a task.
Picture yourself doing it quietly, without announcing it or waiting for thanks. If you pray, offer it as service.

wordCard.voice: Diakonon. The Greek word behind serveth: the one who waits on tables, Jesus' answer to his apostles' argument at the Last Supper. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: the one serving, waiting on tables. The root of the word deacon.

carryVoice: Your line: servant of the servants of God. A pope's title, borrowed from the bottom of the table. Day four hundred eighty, done.
